newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CHEMSERVE UNIT TO SUPPLY CHINESE COIN MINT.
newsitem.headline: CHEMSERVE UNIT TO SUPPLY CHINESE COIN MINT.

text.p: South Africa's Chemical Services Ltd said on Wednesday its Chemserve Trio unit had won a two-year 40 million rand equipment supply and technology transfer contract from the China Banknote and Printing Corporation.
The contract is part of a new coin producing plant for the Shanghai Mint which will produce in excess of a billion one Yiyuan coins a year, the company said in a statement.
The plant consists of electroplating, the associated pre-treatment equipment for the coin blanks, polishing equipment for the electroplated blanks and fume abatement processes.
A new trend in coin production technology was to cover a lower value core of, for instance, steel with a metal such as nickel or copper to produce a cheaper coin.
Chemserve said its unit Chemserve Trio introduced a similar process to the South African Mint in 1989.
The firm added it had fought off competition for the Chinese contract from rivals in Britain and Canada.
